title: A pump with a minimum flow and no rated maximum

blocks.text: A water utility's booster station has one pump. When the pump is idle it moves no water. When it runs, it must move at least `min_flow` (below that it overheats). The station's records give no rated maximum flow, so the flow variable has no upper bound: $`0 \le f`$, nothing more.

`pump_variables` (given) creates the flow $`f`$ and the on/off binary $`u`$. Write `add_pump_rules(model, flow, on, min_flow)` in `pump.py`, with MathOpt indicator constraints, so that the model needs no $`M`$. The tests solve with SCIP (`mathopt.SolverType.GSCIP`), which takes indicator constraints.
The model so far, with $`q`$ the minimum flow:

Write each rule as an implication first ("$`u = \dots \Longrightarrow \dots`$"), then code it. Before running the tests, decide what a big-M version of the idle rule would need that this model does not have.
The tests fix a plan by its variables' bounds and ask SCIP whether it is allowed, so any correct pair of rules passes. Two lines.

from __future__ import annotations

import math

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


def pump_variables(model: mathopt.Model) -> tuple[mathopt.Variable, mathopt.Variable]:
    """The pump's flow (no upper bound: the station has no rated maximum on record) and its on/off binary."""
    flow = model.add_variable(lb=0, ub=math.inf, name="flow")
    on = model.add_binary_variable(name="on")
    return flow, on


def add_pump_rules(model: mathopt.Model, flow: mathopt.Variable, on: mathopt.Variable, min_flow: float) -> None:
    """An idle pump moves nothing; a running pump moves at least `min_flow`."""
    model.add_indicator_constraint(indicator=on, activate_on_zero=True, implied_constraint=flow <= 0,
                                   name="idle_moves_nothing")
    model.add_indicator_constraint(indicator=on, implied_constraint=flow >= min_flow, name="running_minimum")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = mathopt.Model()
    flow, on = pump_variables(model)
    add_pump_rules(model, flow, on, 20)
    print(model.get_num_indicator_constraints(), "indicator constraints")

cases.says: an idle pump with no flow is allowed, and an idle pump with flow refused
a running pump at its minimum flow is allowed, and one below it refused
a running pump may move a very large flow, which an idle one may not

origin.section: Only Some Solvers Take Indicator Constraints

concepts: MathOpt's add_indicator_constraint states that a row holds when a binary takes a given value
HiGHS refuses indicator constraints and SCIP solves them
